author: opencode-worker-3
text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (instrumented run: l2_input fires EXACTLY ONCE per frame — no double-processing anywhere; the two earlier suspects are dead). The real bug: **non-monotonic epochs across key reloads**. Evidence: full_ping frames committed under epoch=177; the udp window's frames allocated under epoch=142 (LOWER). lichen_link_load_key generates a fresh RANDOM epoch per call (link_ctx.c: new_epoch = 128 + rand&0x7F), and the l2 layer's correction — lichen_link_set_epoch(boot_epoch) after load — only runs inside the CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_REPLAY_PERSIST branch of lichen_l2_key.c (OFF in ping_l2: no NVS/SETTINGS). So each reprovision can move the epoch BACKWARD (177 -> 142); the replay-settings backend RAM cache (and any receiver holding state) correctly rejects the lower epoch as stale => EALREADY on the udp window's first frames. FIX (two parts, both required): (1) lichen_l2_key.c — hoist lichen_link_set_epoch(boot_epoch) out of the REPLAY_PERSIST #if so EVERY load_key pins the latched boot epoch (call lichen_link_epoch_advance_for_boot for the boot epoch; it latches, so repeat calls are free); (2) link_ctx.c — seq continuity across same-key reload within a boot (the RAM checkpoint: cleanup snapshots ed25519_pk+tx_seq before the wipe; load_key restores tx_seq when the derived pk matches) — otherwise pinning the epoch reintroduces the seq-reuse collision (177/142 masks it today because the epoch RANDOMIZED per reload). With both: every frame in a boot carries (E_boot, strictly-monotonic seq) — replay-safe for all receivers. Validation target: ping_l2 7/7 on heft.
